candidate_decisions.reason: The five trusted supports (sup_00a89eec9120c614a57c, sup_6e97cdfbee430a78dc3d, sup_aac648eb89917157203e, sup_d2328c8a4a5e76692a8d, sup_f35a36b2b2157acffbfa) describe only the focus surface: humans and jinn gather, bring a likeness, and mutually reinforce one another. They add no independent pericope or host-context trigger, so the proposed aggregate channel is a focus paraphrase outside this macro lane. Its nominated branches are nevertheless landed in other findings: Aty in truth-arrival, received-gift, and spectacle readings; human, jinn, and gathering in the form-bound and commission readings; support in truth-arrival, external-warrant, and the Fatiha aid overlay; general likeness in operation, internal-range, and spectacle readings; represented-counterpart in the 17:93 book analogy.

The exact 17:81 context surface supplies arrival of truth, the departure of falsehood, and its asserted vanishing; the supplied trace coordinates match those forms. The focus's repeated bringing and mutual support provide independent return points. The inference that equivalence includes surviving exposure to reality is bounded and kept qualified.

The 17:78, 17:80, and 17:96 carriers and word indices match the packet's context roots, while the focus explicitly describes mutual parts and backing. Together they support a distinct contrast between reciprocal production support and a warrant supplied by a witness outside that reciprocal group. The protection-and-testimony counter-reading remains live.

At 17:82 the named Qur'an is delivered and has differentiated effects: restoration and mercy for one relation to it, increased loss for another. The focus's two likeness terms supply an independent comparison point. Extending likeness to reproducible operation is an inference, not an explicit definition, and is retained with that boundary.

The 17:84 forms for working, each one's shākila, and guidance match the supplied coordinates. They meet the focus's gathering of human and jinn agents: the contextual rule permits a reading in which aggregation multiplies agents without erasing the formative paths through which each acts. The limit on composition is an attributed inference, with the moral-disposition alternative preserved.

Retain the sequence of received giving (17:85), possible removal and absent creaturely custody (17:86), and mercy/favor (17:87), returned through the focus's attempted bringing and named Qur'an. Exclude only the smallness trace: it states root QLL at 17:85 word 14, but maps to root_001251/B001, whose supplied registry entry is labelled QWL and points to focus QWL at 17:88:1:1. The branch identity does not agree across the packet. The 17:85 context remains landed through the separate giving occurrence.

findings.title: Truth's arrival and the proposed counterpart
findings.claim: The preceding declaration that truth arrives as falsehood departs lets the focus's proposed likeness be read as facing a test of endurance before reality: coalition and support may produce an analogue, while the preceding contrast frames what lacks stable truth as unable to remain.
findings.mechanism: At 17:81:2 truth is said to arrive; 17:81:3 names its stable correspondence, and 17:81:4 and 17:81:9 give falsehood's departure. The focus repeats the bringing verb at 17:88:8 and 13 and grants mutual strengthening at 17:88:19. Their contact changes the challenge from production alone to whether an analogue can persist when exposed to what is real.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hear the preceding truth/falsehood contrast as a possible measure of the attempted likeness, not merely as a separate declaration.
findings.containment: The focus still says that humans and jinn cannot bring a likeness. The durability test is an attributed contextual inference; 17:81 may state a theological contrast without defining the focus's criterion of equivalence.

epistemic.reason: Exact Arabic and context word coordinates verify the carriers, but the claimed exposure test is an inference from a legacy_unbound HFT trace.

findings.title: Reciprocal backing and an outside witness
findings.claim: The focus's mutual backing can aid a coalition's effort, while the surrounding pericope places authority, effective aid, and final witness outside that coalition; cooperation therefore does not itself supply an independent warrant for equivalence.
findings.mechanism: The witnessed dawn recitation at 17:78:14 and the request for السلطان الناصير at 17:80:13-14 place attestation and aid beyond numerical cooperation. At the pericope's close, sufficiency, witness, inward knowledge, and sight at 17:96:2,4,10,11 return to the focus's repeated parts and ظَهِيرًا: reciprocal endorsement can reinforce an attempt but cannot act as the independent witness that settles it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader sees a difference between enough helpers to work together and an authority outside the group by which the attempt is witnessed.
findings.containment: The focus still grants mutual support and still states that the likeness cannot be brought. The surrounding ayat also speak of prayer, protection, and testimony; their use as a criterion of the challenge is attributed and not exclusive.

epistemic.reason: Every trace coordinate matches supplied context roots, but the extension from witness/protection to equivalence-warrant is an attributed contextual inference.

findings.containment: The focus's ordinary comparison remains intact. The inference that likeness entails reproducible effects is not stated in 17:88; 17:82 may describe consequences without setting the challenge's criterion.

findings.containment: The focus still grants real gathering and mutual help. The stronger claim that formed capacities cannot produce a qualitatively new result is an inference; 17:84 may describe moral disposition rather than compositional limits.

findings.title: Received revelation and attempted production
findings.claim: The 17:85-87 sequence can place the attempted bringing in a source relation: revelation is received, can be removed, and remains by mercy and favor, while the focus's coalition tries to bring a likeness of what it receives.
findings.mechanism: The giving form at 17:85:10 returns through the focus's repeated أَتَى at 17:88:8 and 13; 17:86:3 and 5 place removal and hidden conveyance around the revealed object, 17:86:13 denies a creaturely custodian against that removal, and 17:87:2,6 name mercy and favor before the focus asks for production. This sequence changes the challenge from a skill shortage to an asymmetry between received discourse and attempted origination.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the proposed makers as recipients of the very object they are asked to reproduce, within a sequence that locates its keeping and source beyond their control.
findings.containment: The focus's plain challenge remains. The preceding ayat may concern revelation's preservation and the limited knowledge of the spirit rather than define why imitation fails; the smallness branch is omitted because its branch identity conflicts in the packet.

epistemic.reason: The retained word coordinates and HFT roles match their supplied surfaces, but the source-asymmetry link to imitation is contextual inference and the smallness mapping is excluded.

findings.title: One discourse turning through examples
findings.claim: The next ayah's description of one Qur'anic whole varied through every example lets the focus's requested likeness be heard as a counterpart capable of internal range, not only a copy of one specimen; the ensuing refusal can coexist with that abundance.
findings.mechanism: At 17:89:2 the Qur'an is turned through varied modes; 17:89:6 names the same gathered discourse, 17:89:8 makes the range comprehensive, 17:89:9 supplies its examples, and 17:89:10,14 report refusal and covering. These context occurrences meet the focus's repeated مِثْل and change a single-sample comparison into a possible demand for coherent internal variation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive the comparison as involving the range a whole discourse can generate while seeing refusal as a response after examples have been given.
findings.containment: The focus still says that no likeness is brought. The contextual extension to generative range is inferred; 17:89 may be a pedagogical summary after a narrower literary challenge.

epistemic.reason: The next ayah's exact surface and all traced word coordinates are supplied, but the range criterion is attributed rather than explicit.

findings.title: Deliverables beside an equivalent discourse
findings.claim: The requests that follow the challenge can be read as a bounded inventory of spectacular deliverables: springs, flowing water, celestial fragments, ornament, ascent, and finally a readable book can be supplied as objects without thereby becoming an equivalent gathered discourse.
findings.mechanism: The focus's repeated bringing and likeness terms at 17:88:8-14 give the comparison frame. Context 17:90:10 names a spring, 17:91:8 and 11 hydraulic production, 17:92:7 a celestial fragment, and 17:93:6,8,13,17 ornament, ascent, and a book to read. These deliverable carriers meet the focus's distinction between bringing an object and bringing something equivalent. The readable book also contacts the focus's represented-form facet through an explicitly nominated channel branch.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the later demand list as a possible sequence of substitutes for an equivalent discourse, with the requested book approaching the textual form while remaining unproven as an equivalent.
findings.containment: This remains an exploratory structural analogy. The following ayat explicitly present extraordinary demands for signs; they do not state that the list is an inventory of failed copies. The readable book is not explicitly called a representation or equivalent. No claim about the full surah's architecture is made.

epistemic.reason: Exact coordinates anchor every listed deliverable, but reading the post-challenge demands as an inventory and connecting the readable book to a made representation are inferences.
